idea-plugin.name: Antigravity Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Bridges the Antigravity CLI (agy) with JetBrains IDEs (PhpStorm, IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, etc.) so the agent can see your active file, selection, open tabs, and inspection diagnostics on demand.

The plugin runs a small local MCP (Model Context Protocol) server inside the IDE and registers itself in ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json. Whenever agy needs editor context it calls the plugin over MCP — no env vars, no lockfiles, no platform-specific bridges.

Click the Open Antigravity CLI toolbar button (top-right) to launch agy in an IDE-embedded terminal pre-wired to the running project. By default the button focuses the existing Antigravity terminal tab if one is open; enable Always open a new tab in settings to spawn a fresh session on every click.

Exposed MCP tools

  • ide_get_active_editor — current file path, language, cursor, selection, content.
  • ide_get_open_files — every file currently open in an editor tab.
  • ide_get_diagnostics — inspections/errors/warnings for a file.
  • ide_open_file — open a file at an optional line/column.

Artifacts tool window

A right-anchored tool window lists recent brain entries agy generates — plans, summaries, walkthroughs from your conversations. Sorted by most-recently modified so the active session's output is always at the top; the conversation ID prefix on each row helps distinguish entries that share a filename. Auto-refreshes every few seconds while the tab is open; double-click any entry to open it in the editor.

Configure the path to your agy binary under Settings → Tools → Antigravity Companion. No keyboard shortcut is bound by default — assign one via Settings → Keymap (search Open Antigravity CLI) or from the link in the plugin's settings panel.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.4.1

  • No longer writes to ~/.terminfo when the workaround is switched off: the terminfo entry was compiled at project open regardless of the Fix prompt editing in the IDE terminal setting, so a user who had turned the feature off — or who never launched agy at all — still got a file written into their home directory. The lookup is now skipped while the setting is off, and runs when it is switched back on.
  • Settings panel no longer stretches sideways: the hint under Fix prompt editing in the IDE terminal was a single-line HTML label, which Swing lays out without wrapping — it pushed the whole Settings → Tools → Antigravity Companion page far wider than the dialog. The text is now shorter and wraps at a scaled width.

1.4.0

  • Prompt editing no longer garbles the terminal: editing in the middle of the agy prompt used to scramble the display — inserted text landed several columns too far right and the tail of the line was duplicated. agy moves the cursor left with CSI Z (cursor backward tabulation), which JediTerm — the emulator behind both the classic and the reworked IDE terminal — parses but does not implement, so the cursor silently stayed put while agy believed it had moved. agy only enables that optimisation when TERM carries an xterm prefix, so the plugin now launches it under an equivalent non-xterm terminal name (a private agyterm-256color entry compiled into ~/.terminfo, falling back to nsterm-256color). The -256color suffix is load-bearing: the IDE terminal exports no COLORTERM, so TERM is the only signal agy has for colour depth, and a name without it silently drops the palette to 16 colours. Nothing else is lost — 256 colours, alt-screen, kitty keyboard and bracketed paste all still negotiate — and the byte cost is unmeasurable. Toggle Fix prompt editing in the IDE terminal under Settings → Tools → Antigravity Companion if you need the terminal name passed through unchanged.

1.3.3

  • WSL2 support documentation: Added notes to the README and Settings UI clarifying that for WSL2 projects, the IDE itself must be run inside WSL (e.g., via JetBrains Gateway) rather than using a Windows-side configuration. (Fixes #9)

1.3.2

  • Artifact Viewer Fix: Explicitly open out-of-project markdown artifacts in the text editor rather than the default Markdown editor with JCEF preview to prevent blank screens (Fixes #7).

1.3.1

  • Keymap link fix: Configure shortcut in Keymap settings… now navigates to Settings → Keymap within the open Settings dialog instead of stacking a second Settings window on top.

1.3.0

  • Reuse Antigravity tab: the toolbar action (now Open Antigravity CLI) focuses the existing Antigravity terminal tab if one is open instead of spawning a new one on every click. Toggle Always open a new tab under Settings → Tools → Antigravity Companion to restore the previous behaviour — multiple parallel agy sessions remain fully supported by the MCP bridge.
  • Keyboard shortcut: the settings panel now shows the current shortcut for Open Antigravity CLI and links straight to Settings → Keymap for assignment. No default is bound — no chord is safe across every JetBrains keymap, so the choice is left to you.

1.2.0

  • Multi-IDE Support: Generalised branding and internal identifiers to support the full JetBrains IDE family (IntelliJ IDEA, PhpStorm, WebStorm, PyCharm, GoLand, etc.).
  • Critical Fix: Prevented destructive overwriting of mcp_config.json when the file is malformed (Fixes #3).
  • UI Polish: Properly centered and scaled the plugin icon.

1.1.0

  • Artifacts Tool Window: New right-anchored panel to view and open plans, summaries, and walkthroughs generated by agy.
  • Shell Environment: agy now launches within a login/interactive shell for proper PATH inheritance on macOS and Linux.

1.0.1

  • Replaced the deprecated TerminalToolWindowManager.createLocalShellWidget(...) call with the non-deprecated createNewSession(runner, TerminalTabState) path.
  • Replaced the deprecated 4-arg TextFieldWithBrowseButton.addBrowseFolderListener(...) in the settings panel with the modern TextBrowseFolderListener form.
  • agy now runs as the terminal tab's process directly; the tab closes cleanly when the user exits agy.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release.
